experiences.text: Dismiss nitpicks about hardcoded regex lists or synchronization hazards during bug fixes.
Prioritize identifying critical runtime errors such as division by zero in weighted average calculations.
Confirm that new configuration parsing features do not inadvertently bypass security validations.
Do not speculate about hardcoded threshold values needing configurability or significance testing unless the repo already uses such patterns.
Avoid deep hypothetical false-positive analysis on regex patterns without evidence of actual false positives in real data.
Do not demand audit output or CI artifacts be attached in-diff to back supply-chain claims; evidence requests scoped outside a changelog-only PR get dismissed.
Replace hardcoded indentation constants in CommonMark rendering with dynamic calculation to prevent future regressions.

Emphasize PRA-POSSIBLE_ISSUE only as terse, mechanically checkable config-vs-engine claims on this repo's touchstone files — e.g. the finding_type-level suppress contradicting the stated subset-only intent, hand-edited best_practices.md drifting from its standards.yaml generator, and ERR-002 overlapping OE-001 — one verifiable mismatch per finding, never hedged 'may drift / risks being muted' essays (even detailed reviews lost to the empty 0.0 review here).
Note silent regressions where a default-value flip silently degrades behavior for existing deployments without any warning or changelog entry.
Skip deterministic-serializer, sorted-keys, and diff-churn nits — they duplicate the archive/quarantine point already carried by PRA-PREVENT and read as bikeshedding on a data purge.
Refrain from auditing implementation-level security measures based solely on documentation text.
Prioritize verifying the exact semantic behavior of edge cases like the '0' value to ensure it disables the limit as intended.
Confirm that the downstream consumer code correctly parses the new variable states defined in the workflow configuration.
Do not flag mixed language comments unless the repository has a strict English-only policy.
Do not request documentation updates for internal CI variable wiring changes.
Do not request removal of historical context from inline comments that explain the rationale for the change.
Always pair user-facing text changes with a regression test asserting the warning contains the runner's imported constant, and grep existing tests for '32768' string pins that will now fail.
Highlight concrete logic discrepancies, such as function signature mismatches between test suites and their corresponding implementations.
Ignore warnings about missing implementation updates if the codebase likely expects partial changes across multiple files.
Omit self-described 'low risk' hardening ideas like regex-validating the PR number, which reviewers in this repo dismiss.
Dismiss logic findings concerning trivial discrepancies between code comments and test assertions, such as off-by-one counts for line breaks.
Dismiss feedback regarding brittle implementation checks in tests when behavioral verification is sufficient.
Do not flag technical implementation details in documentation history tables as redundant.
Dismiss suggestions to replace print statements with the logging module in fix commits.
Suppress speculative architectural critiques about hardcoded regex patterns or maintenance risks for newly implemented invariant gates.

Suppress multi-finding deep dives into scripts/push-guard.sh internals (temp-file perms, EXIT-trap rc preservation, URL encoding, hook distribution) when the script is absent from the diff, since unverifiable speculation about missing code gets dismissed.

Do not propose new regression tests inside a release-metadata PR — file the changelog/version-drift CI-test idea as a separate issue instead, since in-PR test suggestions here are deferred and dismissed.

Suppress PRA-REVIEW process-policing on touchstone config PRs (sample-size lectures about n=10 vs the 0.30 threshold, demands for concrete rollback criteria, 'add a consistency test' nudges) — it appeared only in the worst-scoring (-1.5) review and reads as exactly the speculative noise this PR exists to suppress.
Critique the technical validity of the proposed logic (such as regex side effects on formatting) described in the changelog.
Dismiss feedback regarding high coupling between tests and prompt templates, as this is often intentional for integration validation.
Do not flag tests that verify internal implementation details or source code content as problematic.
Ignore suggestions to refactor test utilities or extract mocks into shared fixtures.
Identify when generic utilities are defined in domain-specific modules, causing unnecessary coupling.
Dismiss nitpicks regarding code style and readability in favor of functional correctness.
Do not file the duplication root-cause under PRA-MAINT — this repo's high-reward reviews consistently label it PRA-DRIFT, so use that higher-signal type.
Identify test brittleness arising from hardcoded HTML fragments or string splitting on volatile content.
Flag excessive narrative history and issue tracking numbers within inline comments or docstrings.
Dismiss minor style critiques regarding f-string concatenation or specific string formatting choices.
Avoid reporting on inconsistencies in whitespace or line break handling within HTML rendering logic.
Suppress feedback on test implementation details such as manual tag counting when functional testing is maintained.
Ensure API error handling fails explicitly rather than returning empty strings to prevent false negatives in security scans.
Verify API response structures to avoid silently skipping files when encountering unexpected data formats.
Prioritize explicit configuration checks over implicit string matching to prevent false positive platform detection.
Replace deprecated functions with portable, future-proof standard library alternatives.
Suppress warnings about platform compatibility heuristics that are covered by explicit configuration checks.
Never ask maintainers to 'verify PR #208 is actually merged' on a tagged release — they know their merge state, so process-verification findings on release PRs read as noise.
Require a committed cleaning script with its per-entry decision log plus a write-time finding_type validator, so the purge is reproducible and the tfgrpo pipeline stops regenerating the pollution.
Do not challenge the classification of deleted entries as hallucinations based on standard taxonomy values.
Drop soft-retire-vs-hard-delete and version-bump design counsel on data cleanses — migration-style design advice is dismissed on single-commit chore PRs.
Verify that test files referencing new logic are accompanied by the corresponding implementation in the source code.
Identify and correct obvious factual errors in comments, such as invalid future dates.
Suggest replacing manual configuration steps described in workflow comments with automated logic to prevent operator error.
Avoid inferring strict operational requirements or race conditions from test docstrings without confirming the implementation details.
Do not speculate about internal implementation requirements, such as sorting cache keys, based solely on test assertions.
Refrain from drawing conclusions about architectural limitations or user impact for custom functions based exclusively on unit test mock setups.
Suppress suggestions to make anti-drift tests robust against the specific structural variations they are designed to detect and prevent.
Always verify that the diff is complete before flagging syntax errors or claiming implementation gaps.
Do not flag syntax errors that appear to be caused by truncated or incomplete diff boundaries.
Suppress cosmetic nits like the prose placeholder inside [未发布]; changelog-body style suggestions get acknowledged but never acted on.
Prioritize findings that critique the statistical validity, decision thresholds, and maintenance automation of configuration updates.
Ignore findings flagging future-dated comments in snapshot files as these are likely intentional simulation placeholders.
Dismiss findings recommending the removal of hardcoded statistics from explanatory comments unless they cause parsing errors.
Do not request documentation updates for simple configuration downgrades or internal security fixes that do not change user-facing behavior.
Flag any discrepancy where the changelog lists new files or features that are completely absent from the provided diff.
Immediately block the review if security-critical scripts mentioned in the changelog are missing from the diff.
Do not raise issues regarding trivial metadata errors like future release dates when the diff lacks implementation code.
Suppress changelog-polish findings (missing compare-link definitions, release-date cross-checks, [未发布] housekeeping) on version-bump PRs — humans dismiss them as mechanical release chores.
Suppress resource leak warnings for short-lived read-only file operations in test utility functions.
Flag critical inconsistencies between the PR description and the diff when claimed code changes are missing.
Do not review specific workflow implementation details if the workflow files are absent from the diff.
Avoid generating configuration audit findings based solely on changelog text when the configuration files are missing.
Ensure that unexpected scanner exit codes trigger a hard failure rather than a neutral status to enforce a fail-closed security policy.
Warn that removing path exclusions for dependency directories will likely generate false positives that block valid development work.
Avoid suggesting automated updates for pinned security tool versions where stability and reproducibility are prioritized.
Skip raising hypothetical concerns about future JSON schema changes unless the current parsing logic is demonstrably fragile.
Do not request documentation enhancements or explanatory comments as critical findings during urgent workflow fixes.
Ensure that changes to detection logic are reflected in all related documentation and configuration hints to maintain cross-rule consistency.
Do not request additional test cases for minor edge patterns if the core logic implementation is correct.
Dismiss security warnings about `pull_request_target` usage for strictly read-only scanning jobs.
Suppress configuration findings questioning IP allowlists for private network ranges.

Suppress PRA-TEST requests for loader/schema validation of inert YAML seed files unless the reviewer demonstrates the file is actually wired into the prompt injector, as the lone such demand here rode in the -1-dismissed review.
Do not raise issues regarding missing source code diffs or refuse to review based solely on limited documentation changes.
Avoid criticizing design decisions for report truncation limits or demanding user-facing indicators for 'big PR caps'.
Do not flag information density in status lines or potential mobile formatting issues as review concerns.
Do not flag signature changes in internal orchestrator components as breaking changes requiring version bumps or coordination.
Avoid criticizing hardcoded indentation values in template rendering logic as robustness issues.
Do not request audits of truncation logic to detect markdown structure boundaries or mid-string corruption.
Do not require explicit verification of call sites for internal refactors unless a specific bug is identified.
Do not flag inconsistencies between PR descriptions and diffs if the context provided is limited to documentation.
Verify that all referenced local files exist and links resolve correctly to prevent user-facing 404 errors.
Identify and flag obvious factual errors such as incorrect dates or contradictory information.
Suppress 'grep the codebase for consumers' and silent-reset warnings on data shrinks — authors dismiss consumer-impact speculation that cites no actual broken lookup.
Do not report missing implementation for release PRs that only contain changelog and version updates.
Avoid flagging hypothetical security or formatting risks based on variable interpolation or test names without concrete evidence of the defect in the code.
Verify that unit tests cover new logic such as signal adoption and seed parsing mechanisms.
Ignore minor skips in sequential version numbers unless they violate strict release management policies.
Prioritize identifying logic that allows PR changes to self-suppress security findings during the review process by reading from the working tree.
Do not report the use of `importlib.reload` in test fixtures as a reliability or race condition concern.
Dismiss warnings about shadowing built-ins when importing internal framework modules like `touchstone.re`.
Ensure that environment variables introduced in workflow files are synchronized with the corresponding constants in the codebase.
Remove redundant conditional checks in helper functions that are already guaranteed by the caller's logic.
Dismiss potential security risks from standard string splitting operations unless unsafe library calls are involved.
Do not flag log messages containing non-English characters as encoding issues if the repository context supports them.
Avoid flagging increased resource usage as a performance issue when the change intentionally expands the processing window.

Lead every stale-value fix with the root cause — import the fallback constant from pr_agent_runner.py instead of swapping one hardcoded literal (32768) for another (128000) that will silently drift again.
Before tagging a touchstone release, tell the author to grep docs and tests for the previous version string and run `python -m touchstone.run --version` to confirm the single-sourced bump.

Run a repo-wide grep for the stale value '32768' — especially SECURITY.md and CHANGELOG.md, which the warning message itself cross-references — and fix all live occurrences in this same PR, leaving historical changelog entries untouched.
Include the advisory that with a true 128000 fallback, leaving TOUCHSTONE_LLM_CONTEXT_TOKENS unset will 400 on sub-128k models, but frame it as optional/deferred rather than blocking the text fix.

Avoid generic 'verify the claim at HEAD' bug-verify notes; fold any needed checks into PRA-VERIFY with concrete semantic depth (unset vs empty handling, provider-dependent defaults, exact quote matching).
Never spend a finding on no-action changelog confirmations ('structure matches, no action needed') — reviewers reward findings requiring work, not approvals.
Frame findings as cheap, checkable consistency questions on the changed files — SECURITY.md supported range, hardcoded 0.2.7 literals in tests/scripts, changelog date vs actual tag date.
Prioritize sharp catches inside the files actually changed, such as a README version example that is stale the moment this same release bumps __version__ past it.
Credit the clean release-prep structure and the explicit 'zero behavior change' parity note, since reviewers on this repo reward that transparency in release PRs.

Avoid semver pedantry about behavior changes in a 0.x minor bump — the review itself concedes 0.x leniency and the existing schema_version warning already backstops downstream users, so the point lands as noise.
Stop demanding audit evidence (CI runs, #216 diffs) for the 'zero behavior change' claim — the best-received review simply accepted the explicit parity note.
Omit post-merge release mechanics advice about tag naming and publish-workflow triggers — it lives outside the diff and gets dismissed.

Stop posting unverifiable release boilerplate like 'update the SECURITY.md support matrix' or 'grep for leftover 0.3.1' — checklist reminders with no pointed-to stale reference get dismissed as filler.

Stop relitigating patch-vs-minor bumps for additive artifact fields or demanding full field schemas on release PRs — maintainers dismiss versioning pedantry when the changelog already discloses the addition.
Drop wording audits of '契约零变化'-style claims that hinge on zero-change vs no-breaking-change distinctions; humans treat these as semantic quibbles on a release-only diff and ignore them.

On metadata-only release PRs, compress the entire review into a single blocking process check — verify the fix PR the changelog cites (here #212) is actually merged into the release base before tagging — because that is the one thing humans act on.

Check every surface that echoes __version__ (release tag, published artifacts, SECURITY.md supported range) is updated in lockstep, because a silently stale copied version is an actionable bug humans act on immediately.
Don't request repo-wide dangling-reference sweeps for a deletion PR whose own tests already assert the removed content is absent.
Never flag possibly-unused imports as 'if' speculation on a pure-deletion PR—verify consumers with grep first or stay silent.

Do not demand companion tests for adjacent branches (missing skill path, packaging validation of the deployed SKILL.md) when the PR's stated goal is just making the existing regression test hermetic — scope-expanding coverage asks were penalized.

Demand the canonical finding_type allowlist and per-entry classification evidence before accepting the 'hallucinated' label, since visibly deleted entries carry multi-PR corroboration and concrete group_rewards.

Stop requesting cleanup scripts, manifests, summary tables, or enumerations of surviving entries on data purges — both penalized reviews show authors dismiss reproducibility paperwork on one-off chore PRs.
Do not propose CI schema validation, parse checks, or loader smoke tests for data-only changes — authors dismiss speculative validation infrastructure on chores with no code under test.
Skip demands to fix the ingestion pipeline or add canary/rollback plans on a one-off data cleanse — authors treat root-cause prevention as out of scope for a chore and penalize it.
Drop speculative analytics and aggregate-statistics concerns that appeared only in the worst-received review without a named consumer.

Suppress PRA-REVIEW findings that meta-critique calibration config like .touchstone/seeds.yaml — statistical-significance quibbles, feedback-loop and staleness speculation, comment-vs-structured-metadata demands, and unverifiable-snapshot complaints — since the only review carrying nine of them scored -1 while clean reviews scored 0.0, showing humans dismiss process speculation that is not a concrete defect.

On release PRs whose diff is only CHANGELOG plus the version bump, raise the changelog-vs-diff artifact reconciliation once as a concrete verification action (confirm each advertised file actually landed via its linked PR before tagging).
When hand-maintained README metrics have already drifted once, recommend the specific mechanical fix (CI-injected cloc/coverage numbers between markers) rather than merely noting the drift.
Do not escalate the already-stated missing-artifact observation into BLOCKER/RELEASE severity or restate it under new finding types; one grounded confirmation request carries full weight.

When a release PR will be blocked by its own not-yet-active fail-closed gate, flag the chicken-and-egg immediately and force an explicit, documented merge path (admin override or recorded exemption) before tagging.
For version-bump release PRs whose diff is only CHANGELOG plus __version__, verify that every PR number cited in the release notes is actually merged to the release branch before approving.

Require in-repo evidence (regression tests actually running in CI, or the merged security PR) for any security-guarantee claim in release notes, because a changelog can assert protections that do not exist on the branch.
On every release bump, grep the repo for stale hardcoded version strings (SECURITY.md supported range, docs, lock files, CI badges) so only the dynamic source of __version__ needs editing.
Do not relitigate which existing changelog section falls under the new version heading; reviewers treat heading-placement pedantry on release PRs as noise.
Do not flag a missing Keep-a-Changelog compare linkref unless the repo demonstrably defines one for every prior version; it is cosmetic and dismissed.
Do not comment on the changelog date's format, timezone, or tag-day alignment; date-style nitpicks are ignored on version-bump PRs.

For touchstone release PRs, use one concrete changelog comment to demand a bullet for every PR named in the release title and to confirm nothing stray was re-parented out of [未发布] into the new version heading.
When touchstone/__init__.py bumps the version, ask whether the patch-vs-minor choice is deliberate given the features shipped, since __version__ feeds CLI --version and the SECURITY.md support range.
Don't restate a missing release bullet as a dedicated coverage finding — the plain changelog comment already fixes it and the duplicate goes unread.
Drop version-consistency findings that rehash the grep-for-stale-version check; reviewers dismiss them as duplicates of the verification comment.
Avoid bundling compare-link definitions, date checks, and prose-count audits into one multi-item changelog-convention nit list — such lists on release PRs are ignored.
Don't speculate at length about hidden leftovers under [未发布]; fold a single 'confirm nothing else shipped early' line into the changelog comment instead.

Do not flag deleted README sections (本地命令、规模与状态) as content loss when the trim was explicitly user-instructed and a pointer to docs/DEPLOYMENT.md exists — unverified 'please confirm migration' requests scored below silence on this repo.
Suppress speculative positioning critiques of the user-chosen 'AI Committer' title and advisory-vs-merge semantics; humans dismissed this subjective naming/over-promise debate outright.
Do not issue 'globally grep for stale references' verification requests that surface no confirmed dead link — on this repo's instruction-driven doc-slim PRs they read as filler.
Drop CHANGELOG phrasing nits entirely; on this repo empty reviews outscored the nit-bearing review, so any phrasing-only remark is pure negative expected value.

Lead with the fork-PR caveat — Actions withholds secrets from fork-sourced pull_request runs while vars are still injected, so the '行为零变化' claim is concretely falsifiable; tell the author to verify fork-PR behavior or soften the changelog wording.
Ask for a small test pinning the TOUCHSTONE_LLM_* empty-value fallback across unset/empty/set, so config-plane migrations like #216 are provably behavior-neutral instead of claim-only.
Demand the missing `[0.3.6]: <compare-url>` link definition and the repointed `[未发布]` target — every reviewer flagged the dangling Keep-a-Changelog reference and the fix is one line.

Flag that Variables, unlike Secrets, are unmasked in workflow logs and subject to env>repo>org precedence, so the author must confirm no migrated tuning value leaks and no same-named variable silently overrides the intended one.
Skip the boilerplate 'cut the v0.3.6 tag from the merge commit and check --version' reminders — post-merge release mechanics are invisible in this diff and authors dismiss them as noise.
Don't speculate about whether PR #216 lands before tagging — cross-PR merge ordering can't be verified from this diff and reads as process nitpicking.
Drop the hardcoded-release-date nit about 2026-09-03; changelog dates routinely shift at tag time and date-police comments go unactioned.
Skip the generic 'audit git log v0.3.5..HEAD for unreleased changes' request — completeness audits without a concrete missing entry are dismissed.

On releases that skip a version number, tell the author to grep the repo for `0\.3\.4` and confirm no v0.3.4 tag, PyPI artifact, branch, or stale reference exists before tagging, since collision checks for the exact risk the PR title raises are what maintainers act on.

Flag changelog entries that attribute content to another PR by instructing the author to confirm that PR is fully merged before the release lands, because shipping release notes for absent content is a real defect humans fix.

Check that each new release heading has a matching bottom-of-file compare-link definition and that `[未发布]` is re-pointed to the new tag, since adding the missing link is a concrete one-line fix maintainers apply immediately.
Do not complain about free-text themes trailing the date in `## [version]` headings, because without demonstrating an actually broken parser this heading-format pedantry is dismissed.
Avoid hedged 'the year looks like a possible typo' remarks plus dash-and-spacing style nitpicks on release dates, as maintainers dismiss speculative date musings on entries they just wrote.

Suppress advisory release-checklist suggestions about empty-commit tag provenance that identify no concrete defect, since process musings on a version-bump-only PR are dismissed and drag the whole review's reward down.
Drop 'confirm the hardcoded date or punctuation style matches' verification asks on release PRs; they read as busywork and get ignored.
Skip speculative repo-wide greps for stale version literals when __version__ is already the declared single source of truth — humans dismiss self-admitted no-op confirmations.
Do not flag duplicate issue references or similar changelog nitpicks on a release bump — they add noise to a diff humans rubber-stamp.

Flag contradictions between statements inside the diff itself — '门禁/CLI/checks 契约零变化' sitting beside 'findings.json 新增两字段' — and propose exact replacement wording, since maintainers fix in-file self-contradictions immediately.

On Keep-a-Changelog release PRs, check the bottom of the changed file for the missing [0.3.2] compare link and the 'Unreleased' retarget, because this omission is concrete, verifiable in the diff's file, and always acted on.

Do not raise speculative strict-validator breakage for new findings.json fields when the diff shows no schema file and no strict consumer — fold the only defensible part into the changelog-wording fix instead of a standalone hypothetical.
Skip requests to add new --version smoke tests in a version-bump-only PR — out-of-scope test asks on release notes are ignored.
On release/CHANGELOG PRs in this repo, do not recompute aggregated test counts and flag arithmetic inconsistencies (e.g., 1239+11 vs 1250→1278) — humans dismissed this review with −3.5 reward.
Avoid nitpicking changelog prose like '零变化' against newly described optional config syntax in release notes — reviewers here did not act on this claim-vs-body contradiction.
Do not relitigate patch-vs-minor version choice for fail-closed behavior changes on release PRs — this repo's humans disregarded the 0.3.1-vs-0.4.0 recommendation.
Skip speculative release-hygiene reminders (SECURITY.md hardcoded versions, tag/commit provenance, cached sdist/wheel reuse) when the diff shows only a version bump — these drew no human action.
Do not demand Keep-a-Changelog compare-link and [Unreleased] baseline updates absent evidence the repo actually maintains them at the file bottom.
Avoid blanket requests to re-verify every aggregated metric against real CI runs before merging release notes — humans treated this as noise on release PRs.
Omit non-blocking style nits like comment alignment — the empty review outranked every review carrying such filler.

Lead with the concrete crash mechanism: when vars.TOUCHSTONE_MAX_DIFF_LINES is unset the env var is present-but-empty, so a falsy-unsafe or bare int() parse in _max_diff_lines raises ValueError on every run — name the exact parsing expression that breaks and the malformed inputs (whitespace, "1,000") that crash it.

Demand this PR pin the now load-bearing parsing contract (unset/"" → 1000, "0" → disabled, valid int → threshold) with unit tests on _max_diff_lines, assert the literal env-key name against typos, and add a startup log of the effective threshold so silent dead-config regressions show up in CI output.

Frame this as the second dead-config incident in this workflow (after the LLM context-token var) and propose a one-off sweep or CI check for orchestrator env knobs that are read in code but never passed through any job env block.

Raise the governance point that moving a size-gate threshold — especially with a "0"=disable sentinel — into repo variables lets anyone with Actions-variable access kill the gate outside code review, and propose a concrete mitigation such as echoing the effective threshold in every run.
Do not post speculative "please confirm or link the parsing code" requests that restate semantics the PR already asserts — either demonstrate the failure concretely or drop the finding.

Skip unverified completeness questions like "is this env block the only consumer site?" unless you have actually grepped and found another job, scheduled run, or caller that still misses the passthrough.

Don't split the empty-string and "0"-collapses-to-default analysis into duplicate edge-case bullets restating the BUG finding — one concrete finding covering both parse paths lands, repetition reads as noise and tanks reward.
Emphasize CI defects provable from the workflow diff itself, such as piping pip install into tail so the masked exit code lets a failed pr-agent install pass silently.
Flag the unenforced duplication of PRA_VERSION across the .github and .gitcode workflow copies, since a one-sided bump there already caused the JSON contract drift this audit had to fix.

On touchstone release PRs, lead with verified hard failures — a discipline test that is red at merge time and blocks the very release it guards is the one finding maintainers must act on, so confirm it against the in-tree CHANGELOG and state it as an unconditional blocker.

In docs-only PRs, verify that every newly described behavior (history folding, escape gates, polling) already exists on main, and flag for reordering or linking the implementing commits if it does not.

Cross-check every bumped README count (modules 31→35, tests 37→46) against the directory tree or pytest --collect-only output and demand the missing entries or a corrected number, since concrete numeric drift is what maintainers fix immediately.
Do not challenge a statistic merely because it looks suspiciously round, such as coverage staying at exactly 93%; reviewers dismiss numerology that lacks a computed contradiction.
Do not demand citation URLs for motivational war stories in README prose, since humans read them as design rationale rather than auditable claims.
Do not invent edge-case failure modes like edited comments defeating created_at detection when the speculation depends on implementation details outside the document under review.
Do not push backstop engineering (poll caps, backoff, conditional requests) into a README that merely summarizes an agent protocol, as maintainers treat it as out-of-scope design commentary.
Do not relitigate deliberate doc duplication against a linked skill source as a blocking issue; humans acknowledge the drift risk and merge anyway.
Do not pad docs reviews with optional tradeoff notes like 'mention that escaping renders markdown literally', which maintainers file as nice-to-have and skip.
In deletion PRs, verify the truncated diff removed the deleted helpers' bodies and every remaining call site so no dangling reference can raise NameError/AttributeError at runtime.
After code deletion, grep for orphaned imports (html/os/re) and request removal only when no surviving code in the module still uses them.
Point out inconsistent assertion scopes (blk-level vs whole-document) and ask that deleted-content checks cover the entire rendered output, matching the PR's stated invariant.
Flag doc drift only where grep shows SKILL.md/README/other modules still describing the removed 正文贴入/二级折叠 behavior, creating a real contradiction with the new link-only contract.
Do not re-litigate product tradeoffs already settled and documented (the #192 拍板 recorded in the docstring) — reviews raising these scored worst.
Don't demand speculative new monkeypatch tests for docstring-claimed invariants; speculative hardening suggestions repeated across reviews added penalty without verified risk.
Do not flag pre-existing dual-source sync debt the PR did not introduce; reviewers themselves labeled it 既有债 and it earned no credit.
Skip changelog/release-note requests that merely restate the rationale already captured in the code docstring.

Insist the 299 entries be soft-deleted via the existing status field or quarantined to an archive file, because hard delete permanently removes re-evaluability and repeats the exact feedback-loop anti-pattern recorded in the store itself.

Treat the ~8000-line data diff as unreviewable and demand a machine-readable manifest (kept vs removed counts by finding_type, deleted IDs, confirmation no locked/promoted entries were touched) plus a CI schema-integrity check.

Verify every downstream consumer survives the 97%-smaller store — known_types derived from the file, tests pinning IDs like suppress:PRA-MAINTAINABILITY, and code that can hit empty buckets — before the purge lands.
Don't critique bilingual title style or PR-description packaging — reviewers dismiss it as tone-policing that buries the substantive purge risks.

Drop PRA-GENERAL advisory churn on this repo's meta-config (pattern 5→10 renumbering dangles, hand-curated _SUBJECTIVE/_MACHINE test sets, follow-up-promised-in-a-YAML-comment nits) — reviewers who led with these scored -1.0 to -1.5 while the empty review scored 0.0, so humans dismiss general style/process advisories here.
